Load builtin calendars

Source: R/load-buildin-calendars.R
load_builtin_calendars.Rd

bizdays comes with builtins calendars:

load_builtin_calendars()

Value

Has no return

Details

  • actual: every day is a business day.

  • weekends: Saturdays and Sundays are not business days; no holidays.

  • Brazil/ANBIMA: Brazilian national banking holidays, from 2001 to 2079.

  • Brazil/BMF: the same holidays as Brazil/ANBIMA, but it starts in 1990.

  • Brazil/B3: days without a trading session at the B3 exchange, from 1990 to 2079.

This function creates and registers these calendars. Once the calendars are loaded they can be used directly by their names.

This function is called in package .onAttach, so it is not necessary to call it directly. It is for internal use, package development or in situations where the user wants to call bizdays functions without attach the package.

Differences between Brazil/B3 and Brazil/BMF

The two calendars have the same weekdays and settings, and every holiday of Brazil/BMF is also a holiday of Brazil/B3. They are equal from 1990 to 2000. Since 2001 Brazil/B3 has these extra days without a trading session:

  • December 24th and the last weekday of the year (December 31st, or the Friday before it when December 31st falls on a weekend). Banks are open for internal work on these days, so they are business days in Brazil/BMF and Brazil/ANBIMA.

  • The São Paulo holidays January 25th and July 9th, from 2001 to 2021 (except 2020-07-09, when B3 was open). Since 2022 B3 trades on these days.

  • November 20th (Black Consciousness Day) from 2006 to 2019, when it was a São Paulo city holiday only (it was not a closing day in 2020). Since 2024 it is a national holiday and it is in both calendars.

  • 2014-06-12, the opening day of the World Cup in São Paulo.

Up to 2027 the Brazil/B3 holidays come from the calendars published by B3. After 2027 they are estimated by a rule: the Brazil/ANBIMA holidays plus December 24th and the last weekday of the year.

Examples

bizdays::load_builtin_calendars()
bizdays::calendars()
#> Calendars: 
#> ANBIMA, Actual, Brazil/ANBIMA, Brazil/B3, Brazil/BMF, WE-none, WE-prev, actual, weekends
bizdays::is.bizday("2020-01-01", "Brazil/ANBIMA")
#> [1] FALSE
